newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's opposition PSD will not block 97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's opposition PSD will not block 97 budget.

text.p: Portugal's main opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD) will not block the passage of the Socialist government's 1997 budget proposals, the PSD's parliamentary leader Luis Marques Mendes said in parliament.
"We have decided not to block the budget," Marques Mendes said during a parliamentary debate.

"We have decided to let it go through not on the basis of its merit. It is an unjust budget because taxes will rise and it does not fight unemployment. We decided that the objective of the European single currency (which we support) was too serious to risk sparking a political crisis," he added.
The smaller opposition Communist Party (PCP) and rightwing Popular Party (PP) said they would vote against the budget.
The decision of the centre-right PSD not to block the budget means that it will be passed by parliament.
The Socialists have 112 seats in the 230-seat parliament against 88 for the PSD. The remainder are split between the anti-European PP and the Communists.
Parliament is due to hold a final vote on the budget on December 11.
